newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: OLD GUATEMALA STADIUM OFTEN OVERSOLD TICKETS.
newsitem.headline: OLD GUATEMALA STADIUM OFTEN OVERSOLD TICKETS.

text.p: The Mateo Flores stadium in Guatemala City, where at least 82 people died on Wednesday in a tragic crush of soccer fans, is an old building with a history of overcrowding.
At times spectators have illegally packed onto the roof of a stand to watch games, according to a local journalist.
The open-air concrete bowl built in the 1940s is a mile (1.6 km) from the centre of downtown Guatemala City.
New white and blue paint gives Mateo Flores a glossy look from the outside, but inside it is rundown and poorly maintained.
The stadium is designed for a total capacity of 45,000 but there are less than 5,000 individual seats, where wealthy spectators sit in a special area covered by a roof.
Most of the fans cram onto concrete terraces where they sit or stand, depending on how crowded it is, to watch Guatemalan national soccer league games or internationals.
The open stands make it hard to be sure of numbers and easy to overcrowd the stadium.
Hugo Castillo, a sports reporter for local newspaper Siglo Veintiuno, said the stadium had a history of overcrowding.
"The surest thing (about the stadium) has always been the overselling of tickets," said Castillo.
The reporter said sometimes in major games fans created huge security risks by standing on the roof of the stadium over the box seats.
Estimates in Guatemala newspapers on Thursday morning put the crowd in the stadium on Wednesday night at 60,000 or more.

Only two small doors lead to the general seating area in the stands at the south end of the stadium where the tragedy occured. Those two small doors are often overwhelmed as people leave or enter for big games.
One of the doors is at the top of the stands because that end of the stadium is built into a hill putting the entrance at street level, above the playing field.
On Wednesday night the stands were already full at 6.30 p.m., witnesses said -- an hour and a half before kickoff.
But some said the doors were reopened after 7 p.m. and a crush of people came through the small door, setting off an avalanche of bodies in the concrete stands.
Most died asphyxiated, many of them crushed against a chain link fence at the bottom of the stands, around the edge of the playing field.
Crowd control measures at the stadium are also outdated, critics say. Outside, there are no control barriers and ticket holders form wide lines that bottleneck into the doors.

Newspaper columnists and radio commentators on Thursday morning criticised Guatemalans for a "lack of culture" and "lack of manners" that led to shoving and pushing to get into the already full stadium.
But some witnesses blamed the National Football Federation for allegedly reopening the doors, overselling tickets and not cracking down on the sale of forged tickets.
